extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Health Insurance Exchanges, QHP issuers (insurers), agents/brokers/web-brokers, eligibility staff, State health agencies, CMS/OIRA reviewers, and public commenters to the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and comments on proposed regulatory changes to Exchanges and individual market rules (eligibility, verification, enrollment, program integrity, and related information collection burdens) presented in a Federal Register proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process: single application and time estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by the ACA, there is one application through which individuals may apply for a QHP through an Exchange and for other insurance affordability programs like Medicaid, CHIP, and a BHP. Existing estimates: 30 minutes (0.5 hours) to complete for those applying for insurance affordability programs and 15 minutes (0.25 hours) for those applying without consideration for insurance affordability programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses an average opportunity cost (hourly value of time for unpaid activities) of $24.59 and calculates a blended average time (0.495 hours) for affected individuals based on proportions applying for affordability programs (98%) vs. not (2%). The preamble provides numeric burden and cost-savings estimates for affected populations (e.g., net annual cost savings of ~$133,870 and reduction of ~5,445 hours for 11,000 impacted applicants). The agency 'seeks comment on these estimates and the methodology and assumptions used to calculate them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful presence verification: electronic vs. documentation burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on internal data, of 11,000 impacted individuals approximately 80 percent (8,800) would have had lawful presence electronically verified and 20 percent (2,200) would have had to submit supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimates 1 hour per consumer to gather and submit documentation ($24.59 opportunity cost), yielding net annual burden reduction and cost-savings figures when the proposal is finalized. Provides calculations for average annual burden per respondent (0.695 hours) and aggregate annual burden and cost savings (e.g., 7,645 hours; $187,991). CMS seeks comment on these burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to Failure To File and Reconcile (FTR) — §155.305(f)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to require Exchanges to find an enrollee ineligible for APTC after the enrollee or their tax filer has failed to file and reconcile their APTC for one tax year (shortening from the current two-consecutive tax year allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Exchanges on the Federal platform, the FTR process would be conducted similarly to prior iterations except population would be one-tax year FTR and there would no longer be a two-tax year FTR population. CMS anticipates minimal changes to application question language and does not anticipate information collection burden impacts for consumers. CMS 'seeks comment on these assumptions and any information collection burdens not identified.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when trusted data indicate income <100% FPL — §155.320(c)(3)(iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose amendments to specify that all Exchanges must generate annual income inconsistencies when a tax filer's attested projected annual income is >=100% and <=400% of the FPL and trusted data sources indicate projected income is under 100% of the FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimates ~1 hour per consumer to resolve these questions or submit documentation. Estimates ~548,000 household-level inconsistencies across all Exchanges, increasing consumer burden by ~548,000 hours and cost by ~$13,475,320 (using $24.59/hr). Anticipates ~340,000 inconsistencies on Federal platform and ~208,000 in State Exchanges; eligibility support staff will spend ~1.2 hours per verification at $48.34/hr, producing estimated additional government burden (e.g., 408,000 hours and $19,722,720 for Federal platform). Also estimates one-time technical update costs (8,000 hours per Exchange in 2025, with specified labor-cost hourly rates and totals). CMS requests comment on these burden estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove §155.320(c)(5): do not accept attestations when IRS confirms no tax return data
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the rule that currently requires Exchanges to accept attestations (and not set an Income DMI) when the Exchange requests tax return data from the IRS and the IRS confirms there is no such tax return data available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimates large increases in generated inconsistencies (e.g., 1,313,000 household-level inconsistencies for Federal platform and 805,000 for State Exchanges), resulting in substantial increases in administrative burden (e.g., 1,575,600 hours and $76,164,504 for Federal Government; 966,000 hours and $46,696,440 for State Exchanges). Consumer burden estimated at 2,118,000 hours and $52,081,620 annually. Also estimates system update costs (9,000 hours per Exchange in 2025 with detailed labor-rate breakdowns and totals). CMS 'seeks comment on these estimates and assumptions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual eligibility redetermination and automatic re-enrollment hierarchy — §155.335
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.335(j)(4) that allows Exchanges to direct re-enrollment from a bronze QHP to a silver QHP under certain conditions; propose to require that enrollees who would otherwise be auto re-enrolled in a QHP with a zero-dollar premium after APTC be auto re-enrolled with APTC reduced so the enrollee owes a $5 premium instead (unless enrollee submits updated eligibility application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To align with these changes, CMS proposes removal of 'bronze to silver crosswalk' language from Federal standard notices and updates to notices to reflect the $5 premium requirement. Issuer notice burden is approved under OMB Control No. 0938-1254; CMS does not anticipate changes in issuer burden from the notice updates. CMS will revise ICRs to incorporate necessary language modifications and 'seeks comment' on these proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrollment verification for Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs) — §155.420
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.420(g) to require all Exchanges to conduct eligibility verification for SEPs (remove prior Federal platform limit to loss of minimum essential coverage SEP). Also propose Exchanges (including State Exchanges) must verify at least 75% of new enrollments through SEPs for consumers not already enrolled in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimates ~1 hour per consumer to answer associated questions/submit documentation. Historical FFE data estimate ~293,073 new SEP verification issues on Federal Exchange and additional ~179,625 for non-Federal Exchanges; consumer burden increases (~293,073 hours; ~$7,206,665). Staff review estimates: 12 minutes (0.2 hours) per verification at $48.34/hr producing increases in government burden (e.g., 58,615 hours and $2,833,449 for Federal platform). CMS 'seeks comment on these burden estimates and assumptions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Collection Requests (ICRs) and PRA submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Various proposed changes will be submitted for review under OMB Control Number 0938-1191 (CMS-10440) and related OMB control numbers; information collection requirements are not effective until approved by OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS has submitted a copy of the proposed rule to OMB for review of information collection and recordkeeping requirements and provides where to obtain supporting statements and forms (CMS website and Reports Clearance Office phone). CMS requests comments on burden estimates related to each ICR described in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guaranteed availability of coverage — §147.104(i) (attribution of past-due premiums)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §147.104(i), reversing the prohibition on an issuer attributing payment of premium for new coverage to past-due premiums from prior coverage. Under the proposal, an issuer may, to the extent permitted by State law, add past-due premium amounts to the initial premium required to effectuate new coverage and may refuse to effectuate new coverage if initial + past-due amounts are not paid in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS frames objectives as promoting continuous coverage, reducing gaming/adverse selection, improving premium collection, and reducing administrative costs. The preamble discusses potential effects (may deter some owing past-due premiums from enrolling; possible increased uninsured and uncompensated care; potential for more stable risk pools and premium trends) and uncertainties. CMS 'seeks comment' on impacts and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify definition of 'lawfully present' — §155.20 (exclude DACA recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to modify the definition of 'lawfully present' used for QHP, PTC, APTC, CSR, and BHP eligibility to exclude Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provides enrollment and expenditure estimates (e.g., exclude 10,000 Exchange enrollees and 1,000 BHP enrollees beginning in 2025, projected $34.0M reduction in APTC expenditures and $3.2M reduction in BHP expenditures beginning 2026). Discusses expected effects on risk pool, potential transition of many affected individuals to uninsured status, possible costs to States and Federal Government for emergency care, and one-time system update and termination operation costs (detailed monetary estimates). CMS 'seeks comment on these impact estimates and assumptions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for termination for cause from the FFE — §155.220(g)(2) (evidentiary standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to add text to §155.220(g)(2) specifying that HHS would apply a 'preponderance of the evidence' standard of proof to assess potential noncompliance under §155.220(g)(1) and to determine there was a specific finding or pattern of noncompliance sufficiently severe to warrant termination for cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states this codification will improve transparency for agents, brokers, and web-brokers and does not expand bases for noncompliance findings or impose additional burdens on agents/brokers. CMS anticipates positive reaction due to clearer enforcement expectations and 'seeks comment' on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To File and Reconcile (FTR) — restatement and enforcement approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Reiterates proposal to amend the FTR process at §155.305(f)(4) to require Exchanges to determine a tax filer ineligible for APTC if HHS notifies the Exchange that the tax filer failed to file a Federal income tax return and reconcile APTC for any year for which tax data would be used to verify APTC eligibility (removing the current two-year flexibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS frames this as reinstating policy that Exchanges must determine ineligibility when HHS notifies failure-to-file for any year used to verify APTC; references discussion elsewhere in preamble about administrative effects and seeking public comment on these changes.
